#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -t 12h --job-name=Distribution_plots --output=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.out --error=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from --nodes=1)
# -n 4         : 4 tasks (from --ntasks-per-node=4)
# -t 12h       : 12 hour walltime (from --time=12:00:00)
# --job-name=Distribution_plots : job name (from --job-name=Distribution_plots)
# --output=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.out : stdout file
# --error=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.err : stderr file
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID instead of %j
# Note: %x (job name) is replaced with the actual job name in the output/error paths

# Original Slurm partition/qos: general-compute
# Slurm: --partition=general-compute --qos=general-compute
# Note: Flux does not have partitions or QoS in the same way as Slurm
# Performance impact: Job scheduling priority depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or priority settings

# Original Slurm memory: 32000 MB
# Slurm: --mem=32000
# Note: Flux memory specification can be added at submission:
# flux batch --setattr=system.memory=32000M ...
# Or using resource specification: --setattr=system.memory=32GB
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory specification, job may get default allocation
# which could be insufficient for this R analysis workload

# Original Slurm requeue: commented out
# Slurm: ##SBATCH --requeue
# Note: Flux handles job requeue differently through exception handling
# Flux does not have a direct equivalent to Slurm's --requeue directive
# Performance impact: Jobs will not automatically requeue on node failure
# Consider implementing application-level checkpointing for fault tolerance

#module load gcc
module load R/3.5.1

cd /projects/rpci/joyceohm/pnfioric/PDX_RRBS_Processing/Code
Rscript 04_distribution_plots_for_samples.R

# Complete submission command with memory:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -t 12h \
#   --job-name=Distribution_plots \
#   --output=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.out \
#   --error=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.err \
#   --setattr=system.memory=32000M \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification is documented but NOT included in the primary submission command at the top. The initial command 'flux batch -N 1 -n 4 -t 12h --job-name=Distribution_plots --output=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.out --error=logs_bismark/Distribution_plots.{{id}}.err script.sh' is missing the memory allocation. Users must remember to add '--setattr=system.memory=32000M' from the complete command at the bottom.

The output/error file paths use {{id}} placeholder which is correct for Flux, but the directory 'logs_bismark/' must exist before job submission or the job will fail to write output files. No directory creation check is present.
The script changes directory to '/projects/rpci/joyceohm/pnfioric/PDX_RRBS_Processing/Code' without verifying the directory exists. If the path is incorrect or inaccessible, the job will fail.
No error handling or exit codes are checked. If 'module load R/3.5.1' fails or the Rscript fails, the job will exit without clear indication of what went wrong.
The R version 3.5.1 is quite old (released in 2018). Consider updating to a more recent version for better performance and security patches.
The commented out 'module load gcc' suggests it might be needed. If the R installation requires gcc, this could cause runtime issues.
No validation that the Rscript file '04_distribution_plots_for_samples.R' exists before attempting to execute it.
